column1: # walk_promote_scope.tsv -- WHICH PROBES CAN REFUSE A PROMOTE, AND WHICH ONLY REPORT.
# READ THIS BEFORE EDITING. Andy's decision, 2026-09-05.
# THE PROBLEM THIS SOLVES. The promote gate demanded the whole 24-probe scoreboard
# be CLEAN before the customer download could be repointed. But the 24 measure four
# different things at once: whether THIS DMG installs correctly, whether the
# customer's DATA is correct, whether the ARCHITECTURE is what we want, and whether
# the OPERATOR'S BOX is clean. Only the first is a property of the artefact being
# promoted. A build with nothing wrong with it could not ship because contact
# records in another repo had duplicates.
# THE RULE, and it is the whole file:
#   blocking  -> a red here means the DMG WE ARE ABOUT TO HAND A CUSTOMER is
#   advisory  -> a red here is true, and is about the box, the customer's data,
#                another repository, or a design position we have consciously
#                taken. It is PRINTED at every promote and must be signed off.
# ⚠️ THIS IS NOT A LOOSENING OF THE PROBES. Every probe stays exactly as strict.
# What changes is which of them can veto a release. An advisory red is still a
# red, still printed, still in the record, and still counted in the walk verdict.
# ⚠️ FAIL-CLOSED ON THE UNKNOWN. A probe that does not appear in this file is
# treated as BLOCKING by scripts/verify_walk_record.sh. Adding a probe therefore
# cannot silently create an advisory one; someone has to write the row and say why.
# ⚠️ THE BLOCKING SET IS A ONE-WAY RATCHET. It may only ever GROW.
# fails if any probe moves blocking -> advisory. Moving one BACK is the only way
# this file can become a trapdoor, and it is the thing to refuse.
# ⚠️ REVISIT WHEN A LAUNCHABLE DMG EXISTS. Andy's condition on the decision. The
# ticket is CM051 #1508. The intent is that advisory rows get closed and promoted
# to blocking, not that the advisory list is where inconvenient reds go to live.
#   probe   the probe's file name without .sh, exactly as the record names it
#   owner   who can actually close it -- the repo or the decision
#   why     what a red here means, and why that does or does not describe the DMG

column4: the Doctor returned 500 on every load for three builds while /api/v1/sources answered 200, so every artefact-shaped check passed. A customer who cannot open the page cannot see anything, including whether their data landed. A red here is the product.
why
the signature on the .app we shipped. A red is the artefact.
the shipped assistant reaching the customer's own data is the product's core promise. Currently red on 1 of 3 questions (tool_error) and it SHOULD hold the promote.
the prompt is a file in the bundle. A red is the artefact.
the daemon we installed does not answer. That is the install.
shipped tick modules failing to import under the shipped interpreter is the artefact.
a customer-facing surface the install produced.
vendored code failing to import under the installed interpreter is the artefact.

its denominator is WHICH SOURCES EXIST ON THE BOX. safari_history is UNAVAIL on a box with no Safari history, and a walk box is not a customer. A red can mean 'this box has less data', which is not a defect in the DMG.
if the installer lies about its own failures, nothing else in this list can be trusted.
the install did not produce what it declared. That is the definition of an artefact defect.
the bundle we shipped, after first run.
an agent pointing at a program that is not there is the install.
a plist baking a temp path is the install.

54 Person nodes each carry 2+ icloud_contact_uid, collapsing 117 of the customer's Contacts cards into 54 people. That is what a customer sees on the People page, produced by vendored merge logic that ships in this DMG. Reproduced on a FRESH --reset install, so it is re-derived by the shipped pipeline rather than inherited box state. Promoted from advisory 2026-09-05.

promoted advisory -> blocking per LAUNCH DIRECTIVE item 5 (2026-09-07), which made this probe BLOCKING and settled its predicate as REFUSED WITHOUT CREDENTIAL. The row sat advisory for nine days after that and its note still said the probe 'ASSERTS ABSENCE OF A PORT AND NOT A REFUSED CREDENTIAL', which is the opposite of what the code grades: the mapper reads 401 and 403 as refused (pass) and a served uncredentialled request as the defect. WHAT IS ASSERTED NOW: no surface SERVES an uncredentialled client, and every surface that refuses one still serves the install's OWN credential (a lock-out is a defect too). ABSENCE ALSO PASSES, and neither end-state needs the other to exist; both are pinned as self-test cases 25-28. 8044 IS NO LONGER THE OPEN ONE. DECISION_550:106 records it as ABSENT for v1.0 and that was read as 'delete the publish'. Measured: the Hub's Wiki tab reads the DAEMON, which proxies to 127.0.0.1:8044 (ostler-assistant wiki_proxy.rs WIKI_ORIGIN, from web/src/pages/Wiki.tsx WIKI_PROXY_PATH); the daemon is a native LaunchAgent and wiki-site is a container, so unpublishing the port deletes the in-app wiki rather than delivering absence. It now refuses an uncredentialled browser with 403 and NO WWW-Authenticate, so Andy's walk complaint ('the wiki via a browser is requesting authentication details I don't have') cannot recur and the probe passes it on the refused arm. 3000 and 8144 carry the same credential (#1660, #1683). 6333, 7878 and 6379 refuse uncredentialled reads by default. If this probe goes red, a surface is SERVING without a credential or refusing the install's own: both are shipping defects, not design positions.
the install phoning somewhere it should not is the artefact, and it is a security property.
the Hub's own pairing state files disagreeing with its own daemon is the artefact.
a customer who cannot re-pair is locked out of their own Hub.
two of OUR OWN surfaces disagreeing about one number is an artefact consistency defect, whatever the underlying data says.
a write-then-read round trip through our own API.

the two stores hold different SETS of people, and the customer's People page shows one of the two numbers. The divergence is produced by CM041 code that SHIPS INSIDE THIS DMG, so it is a defect in the artefact whichever repo authored the source. Promoted from advisory 2026-09-05 on TNM's argument: 'another repository' cannot cover a writer we vendor and ship. Measured: the 84 orphans are 71 human names with full contact payloads, and 1907-1823=84 is exactly the people_count_agreement gap -- the same defect through two instruments.
what we wrote to disk versus what our own process is enforcing.
a surface the install is supposed to serve.

a run that MINTED the recovery key and never disclosed it produces a customer who can never get back in, and it cannot be repaired afterwards because the key is deliberately never stored. That must hold a promote. Since the redeemability arm was added, two more states block: a passphrase-primary install whose keychain carries no recovery envelope at all (the feature not happening, which this probe used to PASS), and a box holding an envelope that ships nothing able to open one. The skip path -- a keychain older than the run -- is CANNOT-RUN, not a red, so a re-install walk does not block on a disclosure it was never able to make.

ostler-unlock is proven functional but was reachable only from inside a venv, never on a customer's PATH -- the exact class of defect the recovery-key work exists to close. A customer shown a recovery key who cannot even reach the redeemer by name has no path back in, which is the same customer-permanent harm the_recovery_key_reached_the_customer blocks on. Recommended blocking by the PR that added this probe; the classification is open to Andy/Archie review.

three of five required producers live in OTHER repositories and are genuinely unwired there. Also note oa_daemon_chat matches purpose='answering' while no journal record carries a purpose field at all, so that arm has never matched on any box.

A killed install-time converge is a fact about THIS BOX and its data, not a defect in the DMG being walked. install.sh SIGKILLs the resolver at the 300s budget and, since CM051 #1515, records it at ${OSTLER_DIR}/state/dedupe-converge.killed. The probe reads that marker and never the graph, deliberately: the graph is the surface that repeatedly misled the v1067-D002 investigation. It REFUSES (CANNOT-RUN) when neither marker is present, because on an artefact predating #1515 absence is silence rather than a clean run -- v1.0.68 is exactly such an artefact. Promote to blocking only if we decide a customer-visible half-finished dedupe is an artefact defect; today it is a provisional-data warning that every people-reading probe on the same walk depends on.

ADVISORY UNTIL IT HAS RUN ONCE ON A BOX, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE CHOICE RATHER THAN A HEDGE. A blocking probe that has never executed against a real gateway can only refuse a promote for ITS OWN defects, and this one has executed only off-box where it correctly reports CANNOT-RUN. It measures the OPENING turn, ten fresh sessions, the position that failed 4 of 40 in ostler-assistant d791de5f while turns two and three grounded 40 of 40. Its own denominator gate already refuses to report under ten completed openings, so an advisory PASS here cannot be a vacuous one. PROMOTE IT TO BLOCKING once a walk record shows it completing ten openings on a real box: at that point a red is a product fact, and CM051 #2096 names that promotion as the follow-up so it is not quietly skipped.
